name: USB-C socket
summary: The small oval port that plugs in either way up. Needs a 9.5 x 3.5 mm slot with rounded ends.
source: The USB Type-C plug shell is 8.34 x 2.56 mm with fully rounded ends, and that figure is fixed by the USB Type-C specification. Everything else here is not verified: the 9.5 x 3.5 mm cutout is a working opening with clearance added by hand, and the 10.0 x 4.5 x 8.0 mm body is a nominal envelope sized to sit around that opening rather than a measured receptacle. A bare surface-mount USB-C receptacle is nearer 9 x 3.2 x 7.5 mm, so treat the body here as a conservative clearance volume, not a part outline. Panel-mount USB-C modules and pigtail feedthroughs are much larger than this and need their own entry. Note also that a USB-C plug's moulded body is far wider than the shell, so the socket has to sit right at the panel face or the plug will not seat.

keepouts.label: Room for the plug and cable

electrical.note: 5 V at up to 3 A on a plain cable. Higher voltages and up to 5 A only happen when both ends agree over USB Power Delivery.
